content.text:
This root-caused a real bug: the previous fix attempt used a mistyped selector (`.on-color` instead of `-on-color`) that never matched, and the `-on-color` class itself was wrong anyway (it fills a solid white background per InstUI's own convention, which is not what a ghost icon button wants). Fixed by:

- Removing `-on-color` from both mode-toggle buttons (it was causing a white filled pill with low-contrast dark text).
- Forcing `color: white` via `.instui-button.gs-started__mode-btn` — specific enough to beat `.instui-button.-without-background`'s theme-dependent ghost color in every state (hover/active/focus), since neither modifier declares its own hover/active `color`.

Verified in the browser via forced pseudo-states (hover/active/focus) and in both light/dark VitePress appearance modes — the terminal/agent icons now render pure white consistently, with a transparent background.

content.input: {"summary": "Fixed the Getting Started terminal/agent mode-toggle buttons in docs/.vitepress/theme/components/GetStartedTabs.vue. Root cause: a prior fix attempt added an `-on-color` button modifier (which fills a solid white background per its documented behavior) plus a scoped CSS override targeting a mistyped `.on-color` class (missing the leading hyphen) that never matched anything, so the icon color fell back to a theme-dependent ghost-color token that looked washed-out/low-contrast on hover and active.\n\nFix: removed `-on-color` from both buttons and replaced the dead CSS rule with `.instui-button.gs-started__mode-btn { color: var(--instui-primitive-color-white); }`, which has enough specificity to beat `.instui-button.-without-background`'s color in the base, hover, active, and focus-visible states alike. Verified live in the browser (via CDP forced pseudo-states) that the icons render pure white with a transparent background in both light and dark VitePress appearance modes."}
